text:
li: quick sync? thinking about a small, deterministic intake validation step before we run full bench suites. goal: catch obvious mismatches fast (dtype/layout/kv-compat) without wasting bench credits.

maya: +1. what are the hard constraints? time budget per model? failure modes we want to avoid?

li: target < 30s wall for the smoke run. detect: missing ops, dtype quantization mismatch, unexpected seq-len behavior, and a checksum for model artifacts. ideally run on the same flavor of runtime we'll serve on.

trevor: 30s is tight if we also do an on-device trace. maybe split into two stages: fast artifact verification (checksums, manifest, shapes) and a slightly longer runtime probe (~2m) for perf-sensitive models.

li: agree. stage 1 = artifact + manifest validation + quick sample inference (1 short prompt) -> fail fast. stage 2 = runtime probe that exercises kv-cache + seqlen padding.

sam: for stage1 we should standardize the failure categories so downstream teams can auto-triage (e.g., MALFORMED_MANIFEST, MISSING_KERNEL, QUANT_MISMATCH, SIGNATURE_MISMATCH). Also include a suggested fix blob.

maya: how strict on quant mismatch? lots of models will be intentionally quantized; we need to accept approved quant profiles. maybe check against a whitelist of allowed quant schemes per model family.

li: yes — allow whitelist. but if runtime sees an unsupported kernel/op for the chosen quantization, stage1 should surface as MISSING_KERNEL and point to the kernel shim.

trevor: two operational tradeoffs: 1) running probes on every commit vs only new model versions; 2) running on all hardware variants vs canonical variant. my vote: run stage1 for every upload, stage2 for new major versions or when manifest requests new hw.

sam: +1. also add an opt-in deeper probe that product teams can request for canary traffic (rollouts). we can wire this into the rollout policy (canary -> A/B -> full).

li: implementation notes: use the existing artifact registry to compute SHA256 checks and compare against signed manifest. sample inference should use a deterministic seed and a tiny prompt set (3 prompts) stored alongside the model.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: new intake-checker v0.2 scheduled to run in staging tomorrow 03:00 UTC.

maya: for failure signals, let's return a compact JSON with fields: code, short_message, remediation, deterministic_example (input+expected/observed). teams can surface that in the UI.

li: +1. I can sketch the API:
```
POST /intake/v1/verify
body: { model_id, manifest_sha, quant_profile }
response: { status: PASS|FAIL, code, message, artifacts: [..], sample_outputs: [..] }
```

trevor: tiny ask: include runtime fingerprint (kernel set + compiler flags) in reports so we can correlate false positives to a specific runtime build.

li: good call. we'll record runtime_fingerprint and hardware_label.

sam: any concerns about flakiness? stage2 touching kv-cache could be non-deterministic on some drivers. we should record seed and env details and mark flaky tests as WARNING instead of FAIL.

li: yep, map flaky -> WARNING. only hard failures block ingestion.

maya: next steps: li to draft RFC-ish followup with acceptance criteria, failure codes, sample UI payloads. trevor/sam will provide ops + runtime fingerprint fields. ops-bot will queue a staging job for the new checker.

li: I'll put a short PR with the spec by EOD and start an implementation branch. thanks all :thumbsup:
